summary: Intro discovery for PLG/self-serve Redwood API. Hightower wants low friction quickstart, free credits to evaluate time-to-first-token and latency/cost tradeoffs. Key concerns: data residency, VPC/private deployment for later phases, SOC2, and predictable tail latency. Agreed next steps: send quickstart & credits, run benchmark, schedule SE deep-dive.
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Dev Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Hightower Head of ML), Marcus Reed (CTO), Ava Thompson (SRE)

[00:00:10] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Dev our solutions engineer. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into what you're trying to evaluate — quick intro?
[00:00:22] Lena: Hi I'm Lena, Head of ML at Hightower. We've been experimenting with in-house endpoints, mostly on AWS, running some open models, looking to move faster on product features so evaluating hosted vendors and also thinking about a dedicated path later.
[00:00:35] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO. I'll be mostly listening for infra and compliance implications.
[00:00:38] Ava: Ava, SRE, curious about networking and egress.
[00:00:42] Sofia: Great. High level agenda: quick overview of Redwood's PLG quickstart — time to first token, free credits, ease of integration — then Dev will do a brief tech recap, we'll dig into your constraints and timelines and next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:53] All: yes

[00:01:10] Dev: Quick intro — Redwood API supports text generation, chat, embeddings; our PLG quickstart focuses on getting you to first token in minutes using a single curl or SDK call. We also offer Dedicated reserved capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) for later stages.
[00:01:27] Lena: When you say first token in minutes, what's the typical workflow? We want to hand an engineer an API key and have them run something end-to-end quickly.
[00:01:36] Sofia: Exactly — sign up, redeem free credits, grab an API key from the Console, run the example curl we share and you get streaming tokens back. Average time-to-first-token for teams we've tracked is 10–20 minutes from sign-up to sample response if there's no SAML/SSO friction.
[00:01:52] Marcus: Do you support SSO for the Console? We'll probably want SAML for production users.
[00:01:57] Dev: Yes, SSO and SCIM are supported; for PoC we usually give a temporary API key. For enterprise private deployments we integrate with customer KMS and SAML.

[00:02:20] [00:02:20] Lena: Our current stack is AWS, Lambda + internal model endpoints behind ALB, some caching. Our blockers are latency at tail, cost at scale, and security (logs/data residency).
[00:02:35] Dev: Got it. For latency vs cost, we typically discuss batching, KV cache/prefix cache and quantization. Redwood's runtime does inference batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[00:02:51] Marcus: Can you explain the Dedicated vs Hosted trade-off? If we start hosted and then move to Dedicated, is that painful?
[00:02:58] Sofia: It's designed to be low friction — same API surface and tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Hosted is fastest to start (PLG), Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable throughput, Private brings VPC and customer-managed network for compliance. We do support rollouts and model pinning to make the migration smooth.

[00:03:22] Ava: Network-wise, how does VPC peering work? We can't expose internal data to a public endpoint in our default config.
[00:03:28] Dev: For Private deployments we provide a control plane and connector for VPC peering, or on-prem package for fully air-gapped set-ups. For Hosted we mask PII and we have enterprise agreements around data retention, but you highlighted data residency — that typically triggers Private.
[00:03:45] Lena: What's in the SOC 2 package? We need audit logs and key rotation history.
[00:03:50] Sofia: We can share our SOC 2 report and detail audit log retention, RBAC, KMS integrations. I'll attach that to the follow-up.

[00:04:10] [00:04:10] Marcus: Pricing — can you ballpark per-token for hosted and how dedicated commitments change that? We need rough numbers to build a PoC budget.
[00:04:20] Sofia: For hosted, ballpark varies by model class; for mid-sized open model it's X cents per 1k tokens (Sofia: notes to share exact pricing table). Dedicated reduces unit cost and gives predictable throughput; we can propose a reserved GPU pool with monthly commit. I'll send an example pricing sheet after.

[00:05:00] Lena: For the quick PoC we want free credits and a small guardrail: run ~1k requests against a curated prompt set to evaluate latency distribution and quality.
[00:05:08] Dev: Perfect. We typically provision free credits and a sample harness. For latency distribution we recommend streaming enabled and to capture tail latency percentiles. I can prepare a test harness that hits the API with parallel clients, records p50/p95/p99, and toggles batching and quantization profiles.

[00:05:35] [00:05:35] Marcus: Are there any limits on model catalog? We rely on curated open models and sometimes new checkpoints. How quickly can you onboard a new model?
[00:05:44] Dev: Onboarding speed depends on model size and optimizations. For standard open checkpoints we can onboard within a few days; for optimized kernels and quantized variants it might take a week or two. For PoC we usually recommend a Redwood-verified model profile we already host.

[00:06:10] Lena: We care about latency under real user load — concurrent short queries for chat. How does Redwood handle KV cache across requests? We have long-prefix usage.
[00:06:19] Dev: We support shared KV cache strategies and prefix caching — the runtime manages KV state to avoid redundant compute for repeated prefixes. There's also cache hit metrics in the Console. Note transcription: sometimes our docs say "K-V cash" in quick notes, sorry engineers joke.

[00:06:50] Ava: Does the Console show token-level cost breakdown per route?
[00:06:54] Sofia: Yes, per-route and model dashboards, token-level cost, latency, traces. That helps tune batching or route to cheaper model variants automatically.

[00:07:15] [00:07:15] Lena: Security question — if we use Hosted for PoC, is data stored? We need clarity on logs retention and whether content is used to train models.
[00:07:25] Dev: We have clear policies: Hosted doesn't use customer data to train models by default; we can opt-in for aggregated telemetry. Logs are retained per contract, and enterprise tiers include long-term audit logs and full KMS integration. I'll share the security packet.

[00:08:00] Marcus: One of our constraints is egress cost. If we route from our VPC to Redwood, do we pay the egress?
[00:08:06] Dev: Usually the customer pays cloud egress on private peering; we document tradeoffs. For Dedicated in-region, egress is minimized. We'll include network diagrams in the follow-up.

[00:08:40] [00:08:40] Conversation digression about an internal demo they've seen. Small laughter, background noise.

[00:09:20] Lena: Timeline — we'd like to validate within 2–3 weeks and have a go/no-go decision for production in 8–12 weeks. Does that align with typical customers?
[00:09:30] Sofia: Yes, many early-stage PoCs complete in 2–3 weeks with PLG quickstart and credits; Dedicated/private migrations are typically in that 8–12 week window once infra/compliance sign-off is done.

[00:10:05] Dev: For the PoC we'll suggest: 1) Redeem credits + run the quickstart (first-token test), 2) Run the benchmark harness with 1k short chat requests, capture p95/p99, 3) Evaluate quality regression vs your baseline. We'll provide sample prompt sets.

[00:10:45] Marcus: About model variants — if we need lower latency, will you suggest quantized variants? What's the quality cost?
[00:10:53] Dev: Yes, quantization lowers memory and often reduces latency; quality impact depends on model and task — we'll provide quantization recommendation and regression alerts tied to your evals. \

[00:11:30] [00:11:30] Lena: Do you have a self-serve billing cap? We don't want runaway spend during tests.
[00:11:36] Sofia: There are quotas and rate limits on the PLG accounts; you can cap spend at the account level and we can enforce per-key limits. We'll include how to set those in the quickstart.

[00:12:04] Ava: On the networking front, if we go Private, who manages TLS certs and KMS?
[00:12:10] Dev: For Private, customer manages KMS and we tie key usage to audit logs; TLS can be mutually authenticated. We'll share architecture diagrams of the control plane and data plane separation.

[00:12:40] [00:12:40] Mini pause where Sam briefly speaks about data schemas then steps out.

[00:13:05] Lena: What about rate limiting and burst behavior for dedicated pools? Our product needs short spikes.
[00:13:13] Dev: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity options. We can simulate your workload in the benchmark to tune those policies.

[00:13:45] Marcus: Legal and procurement question — do you have a standard SaaS enterprise agreement? We sometimes need custom clauses for data processing.
[00:13:54] Sofia: Yes, we have standard terms and enterprise addenda for data processing, DPA, and security annex. For Private deployments we add platform licensing and support SLAs. I'll connect you to legal if needed.

[00:14:20] [00:14:20] Lena: For the quickstart, can you provide a minimal example in Python and also a curl? Our engineers want copy/paste.
[00:14:27] Sofia: Absolutely — example curl, Node and Python snippets, and SDK quickstart will be in the welcome pack. I'll attach the sample curl that gets you tokens in single request.

[00:15:00] Dev: Technical note — streaming is recommended for chat style latency; we support chunked streaming and function-style responses. For deterministic outputs, you can pin model versions.

[00:15:30] Marcus: Monitoring — what do you surface for debugging high latency requests?
[00:15:36] Dev: We surface per-request traces, token-level latency, queue metrics (if any), cache hit rates, and model-level metrics. There is also an exportable CSV for further analysis.

[00:16:10] [00:16:10] Lena: We use internal eval sets to check for hallucinations. Any integration with evals?
[00:16:17] Dev: Redwood Optimize includes eval monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — we can run your evals regularly and alert on quality regressions as models or quantization profiles change. For PoC we'll run one baseline eval.

[00:16:45] Ava: Do you support VPC endpoints or private link?
[00:16:50] Dev: Yes, for major cloud providers we support PrivateLink/endpoint-style connectivity for Dedicated/Private. We'll note the exact options in the network doc.

[00:17:20] [00:17:20] Quick rebuttal to a question: about model training — Lena asked if Redwood trains models with customer data; Dev reiterates no training unless explicit opt-in. Slight stutter and correction in transcript ("we don't use customer data for model trains — sorry, trainings unless they opt in").

[00:18:10] Lena: Alright, sample plan — can you give us a checklist for engineers to hit in 48 hours?
[00:18:18] Sofia: Yes: 1) Sign up and redeem credits, 2) Run sample curl / SDK to confirm first-token, 3) Run provided benchmark harness on your sample prompts, 4) Share results with Dev for tuning. I'll send the checklist.

[00:18:45] [00:18:45] Marcus: Any gotchas on pricing surprises? We want predictable unit economics for chat at scale.
[00:18:52] Sofia: Unit economics are a function of model size, per-token compute, and cache efficiency. We can model expected costs based on your prompt distribution. The Optimize toolkit also recommends batching and model choices to reduce unit cost.

[00:19:30] Dev: For the PoC, recommend starting with a smaller open model variant to get baseline latency/cost, then test a higher-capacity variant if quality needs it. Also we can toggle quantization to measure quality tradeoff.

[00:20:05] [00:20:05] Lena: Who from Redwood will own the PoC?
[00:20:09] Sofia: I'll own the relationship as AE, Dev will be technical lead for the PoC. For network/procurement we'll loop in Solutions Engineering and Legal as needed.

[00:20:30] Ava: Can you share a sample architecture diagram of Private? I'd like to circulate to our infra folks.
[00:20:36] Dev: Yes, I'll include the Private control plane diagram and example VPC peering steps.

[00:21:00] [00:21:00] Short silence, typing sounds.

[00:21:30] Lena: Anything else we should know about limits on quickstart? Token caps?
[00:21:36] Sofia: Quickstart accounts have initial quota and rate limit; we'll set a PoC quota for you so there's no surprise billing. The free credits plus a quota cap gives you a safe sandbox.

[00:22:10] Marcus: If we later go Dedicated, do you recommend a staged migration or big-bang? We want minimal downtime.
[00:22:19] Dev: Staged is better: run both in parallel, route a percentage to Dedicated via Canary, then cutover. Redwood Console supports rollouts, A/B tests and automatic fallback.

[00:22:50] [00:22:50] Lena: Great — let's recap next steps at high level.
[00:22:54] Sofia: Recap: we'll provision free credits and send quickstart + sample curl + Python snippet; Dev will prepare benchmark harness and a sample prompt set; Redwood will share SOC2 and network diagrams; Hightower to provide compliance contacts and confirm timelines.

[00:23:15] Marcus: That works. Please also include an estimated price range for hosted PoC and an example Dedicated commit to compare.

[00:23:25] Sofia: Will do.

[00:24:00] [00:24:00] Short technical aside where Dev mentions a kernel optimization for attention that reduced latency in a customer's benchmark, slight technical jargon and "KV cache" said a few ways.

[00:25:10] Lena: Logistics — Sprint cycles align, we'll have engineers available for the PoC next week. Interested in a joint runbook session.

[00:25:18] Dev: We'll schedule a runbook session during the benchmark week; likely pair-program with one of your engineers.

[00:26:00] [00:26:00] Quick Q&A about tokenization differences between models — Dev gives short answer and says sample code will include tokenizer notes.

[00:26:40] Lena: Any references or case studies of customers of similar size?
[00:26:45] Sofia: Yes, we'll share a short case study of a mid-market SaaS that used PLG quickstart and later migrated to Dedicated for predictable SLOs. I'll attach that.

[00:27:10] [00:27:10] Short pause, light background noise.

[00:27:45] Marcus: For procurement, what's the expected lead time for Dedicated?
[00:27:51] Sofia: From signed contract to reserved capacity typically 4–8 weeks depending on cluster scheduling and region. We can aim for the lower bound if you have flexibility.

[00:28:20] Dev: Also note that for Dedicated we offer autoscaling policies and burst capacity so small spikes are covered while optimizing for cost.

[00:29:00] [00:29:00] Lena: Ok, action items again? We want owners.
[00:29:05] Sofia: I'll send the list — but quick: Sofia send docs and credits; Dev build the harness; Lena provide compliance contact; Ava confirm egress needs.

[00:29:30] Marcus: Sounds good.

[00:30:00] [00:30:00] Final clarifying questions about metrics export formats. Dev says JSON/CSV supported.

[00:31:10] Lena: Anything else on your side?
[00:31:14] Sofia: Nothing else — we'll follow-up with the materials and link to redeem credits.

[00:31:30] [00:31:30] Closing: thanks all, Sofia and Dev sign off, Hightower team confirm next week's PoC kickoff.

[00:32:00] Post-call internal note (Sofia to self, not read aloud): Give them 5k credits, include sample 1k request harness, propose 2-hour runbook pairing session 2026-03-10.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and filler speech, speaker overlaps, and short crosstalk. References to external artifacts: Quickstart guide (link: https://redwood.ai/quickstart - note: placeholder), Benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/poс-benchmark - note: placeholder), SOC2 packet (attached in follow-up).
